text: . World Toilet Day is being observed today. Observed since 2013, the day is an official United Nations observance aimed at raising global awareness and action to address the urgent sanitation crisis. It has been dedicated to emphasizing the importance of safe and accessible toilet facilities as part of Sustainable Development Goal 6: Ensuring water and sanitation for all by 2030.This year’s theme is Safe toilets. Equal futures. It highlights how safe sanitation protects women and girls’ health, safety, dignity and opportunity, enabling them to go to school, work and fully take part in society. The day was established to shed light on the challenges faced by billions worldwide due to inadequate sanitation. The observance underscores the indispensable role of proper toilet facilities in maintaining public and environmental health by preventing the spread of deadly diseases such as cholera.

. Around 1,000 tourists have been stranded on St Martin’s Island in Bangladesh after authorities suspended vessel services on the Cox’s Bazar-St Martin’s route due to rough seas triggered by Cyclone Akvan in the Bay of Bengal. According to local media reports, the tourists had arrived on November 17 and 18 and are unable to return until weather conditions improve.The Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority suspended all vessel operations from Thursday following a warning from the Bangladesh Meteorological Department for maritime ports.Authorities said services would resume only after conditions become favourable, prioritising passenger safety. Meanwhile, tourists holding advance tickets have been assured of either rescheduled travel or refunds.

. Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) Jitan Ram Manjhi today inaugurated the MSME Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair 2026 in New Delhi. On the occasion, Mr Manjhi interacted with artisans and exhibitors at various stalls. He highlighted the importance of khadi as a symbol of country’s rich cultural heritage and traditional craftsmanship. The Minister said that khadi represents country’s traditional industry, entrepreneurship and art. Mr Manjhi also highlighted the PM Vishwakarma Yojana, which covers 18 traditional trades, including barbers, leather artisans, cobblers, garland makers and net weavers.

. Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush of Diwali and Chhath Puja, with extensive crowd management preparations underway at several railway stations. Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing dedicated passenger holding areas, known as Yatri Suvidha Kendras, at major railway stations across the country. This is being done to streamline passenger movement and ease congestion during periods of heavy footfall, including the festive season. The Yatri Suvidha Kendras, or Passenger Holding Areas, are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers. Our correspondent reports that the facilities have been designed to ensure orderly passenger movement and provide a comfortable waiting environment.The holding areas have been designed to accommodate passengers before they proceed to the platform area. Talking to Akashvani News, Northern Railway CPRO  said that at New Delhi Railway station, a holding area is available for both reserved and unreserved classes. He said additional RPF personnel have also been deployed at Railway stations to facilitate passengers.At Anand Vihar Terminal, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra has 14 ticket counters, 16 CCTV cameras, four electronic display boards and seating for 20 passengers. The facility also has separate toilet facilities for male and female passengers, a Divyangjan toilet, an RO plant, 11 HVLS fans and a public announcement system. The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms, in circulating areas and at station approaches by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing.

. Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth visited the General Staff Headquarters of the Czech Armed Forces in Prague during his official visit to the Czech Republic, holding discussions with senior military leaders on strengthening bilateral defence cooperation and professional military exchanges.During the visit, Gen Seth laid a wreath in a solemn ceremony to honour soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice in service of their country. He also called on Lieutenant General Petr Cepelka, First Deputy Chief of the General Staff, with discussions focusing on the evolving security environment and opportunities to deepen defence ties.The Army Chief was briefed on ‘Horizon 2035: Land Warfare Modernisation and Future Readiness of the Czech Armed Forces’, covering future warfare, technological transformation and operational preparedness. As part of his remaining engagements, Gen Seth is scheduled to call on senior officials of the Czech Ministry of Defence to discuss military cooperation, training, modernisation and emerging security challenges.

. Talismanic former India captain Mahendra Singh Dhoni’s playing career in the IPL ended today after he was appointed the mentor of his franchise Chennai Super Kings. Team co-owner Rupa Gurunath revealed that MS Dhoni expressed his desire to retire during a call to decide retained players for the upcoming season. She said, Dhoni will continue to be a part of the CSK family as a mentor. She added that with many youngsters in the squad, his guidance will help shape the next generation of CSK. The superstar wicketkeeper-batter had announced retirement from international cricket in 2020.

. The 45th Indian International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 will begin tomorrow at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Talking to media, Chairman of India Trade Promotion Organisation, Jawed Ashraf said that this year the focus is on three key aspects that are enhancing the visitor experience, showcasing innovations and highlighting India’s rich heritage. He said that visitors can book tickets online through the IITF 2026 mobile application, which is integrated with the DMRC’s Sarthi app. Mr Ashraf informed that shuttle bus services will operate from several metro stations, including Mandi House, connecting visitors to all entry gates of the venue. Visitors can also reach Bharat Mandapam through app-based taxis, private vehicles and public transport. He added that parking facilities for around three thousand vehicles have been arranged, along with designated waiting areas for app-based taxis. Special facilities, including wheelchair assistance will also be available for senior citizens to ensure a comfortable and convenient experience.

. The Women’s Asian Champions Trophy 2026 hockey tournament will begin in Bhopal tomorrow. The tournament will continue till 28th of this month. Apart from India, teams from China, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia and Thailand will participate in the tournament. India has won this title three times in 2016, 2023 and 2024. India will begin its campaign against Malaysia tomorrow. The match will start at 7 PM.Recently, the Indian women’s hockey team defeated China to win the gold medal at the 2026 Asian Games after 44 years. With this victory, the team also qualified for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The Asian Champions Trophy will be country’s first international tournament after its Asian Games victory.All six teams will play against each other in the league stage. Each team will play five matches, and the top four teams in the points table will qualify for the semi-finals. League matches will be held from 19th to 25th September. Both semi-finals and the match for fifth place will take place on 27th of this month. The bronze medal match and the final will be played on 28th of this month.India will face South Korea on 21st November, Thailand on 22nd, and China on 24th November. The Indian team will play its final league match against Japan on 25th November.

. Bangladeshi actress Jyotika Jyoti was arrested by the Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police early Thursday from her residence in Uttara, the capital. Police detained her around 2:45 am from a government residential quarter in Sector 18, under Turag Police Station, and took her to the DB office on Minto Road for questioning.Before her arrest, Jyoti went live on Facebook several times, claiming police had arrived at her home without an arrest warrant. DB officers reportedly broke down her door to enter the residence. Police said several cases had been filed against her and alleged links with the activities of the banned Awami League. However, officials did not immediately disclose the specific charges.

. Union Minister for Jal Shakti C. R. Patil has stressed the need for integrated management of rivers, reservoirs and dams to strengthen the country’s water security. He was speaking at the inauguration of a national conference organised jointly by the Central Water and Power Research Station (CWPRS) and the Indian Society for Hydraulics at Khadakwasla in Pune.Highlighting the challenges posed by climate change, including heavy rainfall and floods, the Minister emphasised the importance of ensuring the safety of ageing dams, addressing silt accumulation in reservoirs and improving water management. He called for effective use of Artificial Intelligence, digital technology, modern surveying techniques and scientific research to address these challenges.The two-day conference brings together engineers, scientists, water resources experts and policymakers from across the country to deliberate on integrated river basin management, flood control, dam safety and reservoir sediment management.Secretary of the Department of Water Resources Archana Verma and CWPRS Director Dr M. Selva Balan were among those present. Technical publications on riverbank protection, structural inspection of dams using remotely operated vehicles and water project studies were released on the occasion.Models of the Dibang Multipurpose Project and Kaleshwaram Lift Irrigation Scheme were also inaugurated. Memoranda of Understanding for research collaboration were exchanged between CWPRS and the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, Bhakra Beas Management Board and Brahmaputra Board.

. In the forex market today, the rupee appreciated marginally by to close at 93 rupees and 45 paise against the US dollar. The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 103.82 in intra-day trade.

. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today chaired the second Pre-Budget Consultation meeting with experts from agriculture and rural development sectors ahead of the forthcoming General Budget 2027-28 in New Delhi. The Pre-Budget consultation meeting was also attended by Secretaries of Department of Economic Affairs, Anuradha Thakur, Secretary of Department of Fisheries, Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi and senior officials of Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.Earlier in the day, the Finance Minister chaired the first Pre-Budget Consultation with leading economists in connection with the upcoming Union Budget 2027-28, in New Delhi. The meeting was also attended by Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs, Anuradha Thakur and Chief Economic Adviser, Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran and senior officers from the Department.The Finance Ministry conducts several pre-Budget consultation meetings annually with experts, industry leaders, economists, and state officials. The deliberations seek to ensure the Union budget reflects diverse perspectives and addresses key economic priorities.

. The Health Ministry has proposed an amendment to the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019, to include ‘antimicrobials’ in the definition of ‘New Drug’. It has been proposed with a view to strengthening regulatory oversight and addressing the growing threat of antimicrobial resistance AMR. The Ministry said antimicrobial resistance is a major global public health concern and a priority that requires coordinated action.The G20 New Delhi Leaders’ Declaration also underscored the need to address AMR through a One Health approach. According to the Ministry, the proposed amendment has been initiated in view of concerns over the grant of manufacturing licences for antimicrobial products without adequate regulatory scrutiny, including assessments such as bioavailability, bioequivalence and stability studies. It said that the absence of these assessments could compromise the quality, safety and efficacy of antimicrobial products.The Ministry noted that substandard or ineffective antimicrobials could contribute to the emergence and spread of antimicrobial resistance, thereby posing risks to patient safety and public health. Under the proposed amendment, antimicrobials would be brought within the regulatory framework applicable to new drugs under the 2019 Rules. Consequently, manufacturers would be required to obtain prior permission from the Central Licensing Authority before applying to the concerned State Licensing Authority for a manufacturing licence. The move is expected to strengthen central regulatory oversight and ensure that antimicrobial products meet the requisite standards of quality, safety and efficacy before being permitted for manufacture.The Ministry has issued a draft notification inviting objections and suggestions from stakeholders and members of the public before the proposed amendment is considered for finalisation by the Central Government. Objections and suggestions, if any, may be submitted to the Under Secretary (Drugs), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, or emailed to drugsdiv-mohfw@gov.in, within 30 days from the date on which copies of the Gazette containing the draft rules are made available to the public.

The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare’s dedicated Health Pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 in New Delhi is showcasing its flagship health programmes and public healthcare initiatives. The theme of this year’s Health Pavilion is Yuva Bharat, Swasth Bharat, highlights preventive healthcare, healthy lifestyles and youth participation in building a healthier nation. The Pavilion was inaugurated by NITI Aayog Member, Dr M Srinivas, in the presence of Health Secretary, Punya Salila Srivastava.Addressing the gathering, Dr. Srinivas emphasised on preventive healthcare and healthy lifestyle choices to address rising burden of Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs) and lifestyle-related health conditions. He also highlighted the importance of public awareness, early detection and timely medical intervention in preventing and managing NCDs. Outlining the benefits of Health Pavilion, Dr. Srinivas said that it offers a valuable opportunity for citizens to learn about common health risks, understand preventive measures and familiarise themselves with various Government healthcare programmes and services. He also encouraged visitors to actively participate in the Pavilion’s activities and use the opportunity to enhance their understanding of health and well-being.The Ministry noted that in the Pavilion 39 stalls representing 24 national health programmes and organisations showcase Government’s healthcare initiatives, achievements and services. The Ministry also highlighted that a dedicated TB stall has been established to raise awareness about tuberculosis and TB screening is being conducted using AI-enabled handheld X-ray technology. The Pavilion also included interactive activities, live cpr demonstrations, health awareness sessions and dedicated kids’ zone to engage visitors and promote healthy living. The Ministry said that the Pavilion provides an important platform to connect directly with citizens, showcase the Government’s wide-ranging healthcare initiatives and promote greater public awareness about preventive healthcare, early diagnosis and healthier lifestyles.

. Major Asian stock market indices ended on a mixed note today. South Korea’s Kospi rose two per cent, Japan’s Nikkei 225 gained 0.3 per cent, Taiwan’s Taiex added nearly 0.3 per cent and China’s Shanghai Composite added 0.1 per cent. Conversely, Singapore’s Strait Times fell 1.1 per cent, and Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dropped 0.9 per cent.In European markets, London’s FTSE 100 dipped 0.4 per cent while, Germany’s DAX eked out a marginal gain, when reports last came in.On the economic front, inflation rate in the United Kingdom rose to a one year high of 3.6 per cent in October on an annual basis, up from 3.5 per cent in September, according to the data released by the government . The core Consumer Price Index (CPI) which excludes food, energy, alcohol, and tobacco stood at 2.8 per cent year-on-year, unchanged from September.

. Chief of Defence Staff General N S Raja Subramani has said that Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) is an expression of India’s commitment to human security, both within the country and across its wider neighbourhood. General Subramani was addressing the media at the Jamnagar Air Force Station on the third and concluding day of the Annual Joint Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief Exercise 2026 –   Exercise Sahayata Setu, which commenced on Tuesday.The Chief of Defence Staff observed that in today’s disaster-prone world, an effective response cannot be the responsibility of any one agency alone, as it requires a coordinated, whole-of-nation approach involving the government, defence forces, NDRF, other agencies and citizens. He said, in 2016, Prime Minister Narendra Modi had emphasised disaster risk reduction through his Ten-Point Agenda, and the underlying principle is that preparedness must be collective, response must be coordinated, and no effort should be spared in saving precious lives.General N S Raja Subramani emphasised that Exercise Sahayata Setu 2026 is an important step towards translating this vision into reality. It brings together the three services, the Indian Coast Guard, NDMA, NDRF, state and civil administrations, along with friendly foreign countries, to strengthen a common approach to disaster response. He said, India’s approach to Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Response is guided by the Neighbourhood First Policy and the vision of MAHASAGAR(Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions).He highlighted that India is a dependable first responder in the Indian Ocean Region as well as across the wider Indo-Pacific. He said India’s experience in Operation Dost in Türkiye and Operation Brahma in Myanmar demonstrates its ability to mobilise and deliver assistance across borders in a timely and coordinated manner.

Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman today chaired the sixth Pre-Budget Consultation with the experts and stakeholders from the Information Technology sector in connection with the forthcoming Union Budget 2027-28, in New Delhi. The meeting was also attended by Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs, Anuradha Thakur, CEO of NITI Aayog, Anurag Jain and Chief Economic Adviser Dr V. Anantha Nageswaran. Senior officials from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology also attended the meeting.The Finance Ministry conducts several pre-Budget consultation meetings annually with experts, industry leaders, economists, and state officials. The deliberations seek to ensure the Union budget reflects diverse perspectives and addresses key economic priorities.

. India’s overall unemployment rate declined by 0.3 per cent to 4.9 per cent in October on an annual basis. According to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation’s periodic labour force survey bulletin, the rural unemployment rate fell to 4.2 per cent and urban unemployment rate decreased to 6.7 per cent last month. Worker Population Ratio (WPR) increased by half a per cent to 53 per cent in October on an annual basis. WPR in rural areas increased to 58.4 per cent last month, while in urban areas it remained unchanged at 50.5 per cent on a year-on-year basis. Among female, WPR rose to 33.3 per cent in October. Meanwhile, the male WPR remained largely unchanged at 73.7 per cent over the same period.The overall Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) among persons of age 15 years and above grew by 0.3 per cent to 55.7 per cent last month on an annual basis.

. IndiGo has cancelled all its flights to and from four major Saudi Arabian cities, Jeddah, Madinah, Riyadh and Dammam until November 30, in view of the prevailing security situation.The airline said the cancellations would remain in effect until November 30. The airline said affected passengers are being informed through Airline’s registered contact details and assured that necessary assistance would be provided. IndiGo said the safety and security of passengers and crew remain its highest priority.The development comes amid rising security concerns after the Saudi-led coalition reportedly intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by Yemen’s Houthi rebels towards southern Saudi Arabia. Saudi authorities had also briefly issued emergency alerts for Abha City and Khamis Mushait in the southwestern region, which were later withdrawn after the danger had passed.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has welcomed the growing momentum in India-UK relations, guided by the India-UK Vision 2035 and further strengthened by the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), which came into force in July this year.Prime Minister Modi said this during his meeting with the Prince and Princess of Wales in New Delhi yesterday. Prime Minister Modi commended the work of the Earthshot Prize in encouraging innovative solutions to pressing environmental challenges. He appreciated its recognition of Indian innovators and their contributions to addressing global environmental challenges, including at the Earthshot Prize Awards held in Mumbai yesterday.The meeting also provided an opportunity to exchange views on further strengthening the India-UK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, including cooperation in defence, health, education, fin-tech and people-to-people ties. Mr Modi also conveyed his warm regards to King Charles III and to Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

. The Women’s Asian Hockey Champions Trophy 2026 started today at the International Sports Complex in Nathu Barkheda, Bhopal. China and Thailand are playing the opening match of the tournament. The match is currently underway. Japan and South Korea will play the next match at 2:20 PM. The third match of the day will be between host India and Malaysia at 4:35 PM.The championship will be held from November 19 to 28. Six teams: India, China, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia and Thailand are taking part in the tournament. The Indian team is entering the competition as the defending champion. India has won this title three times and will aim to win its fourth trophy this year.The Indian team has won the FIH Nations Cup this year and also qualified for the World Cup. The team also made history by winning the gold medal at the Asian Games after a gap of 44 years. The tournament will follow a round-robin format, where every team will play against the other teams. The top four teams will qualify for the semi-finals. The semi-final matches will be played on November 27, while the final will take place on November 28.

. India’s electronic goods exports registered strong growth of 44 per cent during April-September this fiscal year, increasing from over 22 billion dollars in the corresponding period of 2025-26 to around 32 billion dollars. While smartphones continued to account for the largest share of the electronics export basket, non-smartphone electronics recorded significantly faster growth, reflecting the broadening and diversification of India’s electronics exports across components, printed circuit boards, communication equipment, memory products and storage devices.Exports of smartphones increased by over 35 per cent, from 13 billion dollars in April-September last year to over 18 billion dollars during April-September this year. Smartphones continued to be the largest component of India’s electronic goods exports. However, their share in total electronic goods exports moderated from 60.3 per cent to 56.8 per cent, amid faster growth in other electronics segments.Non-smartphone electronics exports recorded a growth of over 56 per cent, increasing from around nine billion dollars to over 13 billion dollars during the period. The share of non-smartphone electronics in total electronic goods exports increased from 39.7 per cent to 43.2 per cent, indicating a broadening of India’s electronics export basket.Exports of parts and accessories comprising mounted printed circuit boards increased from over 63 million dollars to over two billion dollars registering growth of 3219 per cent. Singapore was the leading destination, with exports reaching 1.87 billion dollars, followed by China at 111.5 million dollars.

. In badminton, Indian men’s doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty stormed into the quarterfinals of the Hong Kong Open Super 500 badminton tournament today. The Indian duo defeated Malaysia’s Nur Mohd Azriyn Ayub and Tan Wee Kiong with a straight-game win 21-19, 21-16. Satwik and Chirag will next face China’s Hu Ke Yuan and Lin Xiang Yi, who beat Japan’s Kakeru Kumagai and Hiroki Nishi 21-19, 21-17.On the other hand, India’s Lakshya Sen will take on Denmark’s Rasmus Gemke in the men’s singles pre-quarterfinals later in the day.In the women’s doubles, Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, the bronze medallist at the World Championships in New Delhi, lost to the American pair of Lauren Lam and Allison Lee 20-22, 13-21 in the pre-quarterfinals to end their campaign

. In Badminton, the Indian Men’s Doubles pair of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty advanced to the second round of Hong Kong Super 500 tournament today. The star Indian pair defeated Chinese Taipei’s Lee Jhe-huei and Yang Po-han, 15-21, 21-17, 28-26 in their opening round match.Earlier in the day, Indian mixed doubles pair of Dhruv Kapila and Radhika Sharma progressed to the main draw of the tounramnet with a straight-game win. They took just 36 minutes to beat Hong Kong’s Cheng Ying Kit and Leung Yuet Yee, 21-17 21-17.Indian Shuttlers Lakshya Sen and Kidambi Srikanth will begin their campaign in Men’s Singles tomorrow.

. Global crude oil prices displayed a mixed trend today. Brent crude was trading marginally up at 93 US dollars and 18 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading half a per cent down at 84 US dollars and 21 cents per barrel.

. Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr Virendra Kumar today inaugurated the Shilp Samagam Mela 2026 at Dilli Haat, INA in New Delhi this evening. The Mela will provide a dedicated marketing platform to artisans and beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, Safai Karamcharis and persons with disabilities to showcase and market their products to a wider audience. Speaking on the occassion, Dr Kumar said the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment has been organising Shilp Samagam Melas since 2022 and more than 1,000 artisans from Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes and Safai Karamcharis have benefited from opportunities to exhibit and market their products.  The Minister said that with approximately 150 stalls for participating male and female artisans to showcase their handicraft and handloom products under Bharat TULIP and Purple Fest, the initiative brings traditional artisans, creative talent and persons with disabilities together on a common platform to encourage wider market access and equal opportunities for participation.  The Mela will remain open to visitors until 15th of this month.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow.The Met Department has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Kerala, Mahe and Lakshadweep during the next two days. Similar conditions are expected over Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura tomorrow.Meanwhile, the weather agency has forecast mist and shallow fog at most places of Delhi during the morning hours tomorrow.The air quality in Delhi-NCR is in the ‘ Very Poor’ category. According to the Central Pollution Control Board, Delhi’s Air Quality Index was recorded at 303 as of 7 PM today.

. Three major works of India’s literary and intellectual heritage including Kalhana’s Rajatarangini, the Mahabharata and Kautilya’s Arthashastra have been included in UNESCO’s Memory of the World Regional Register for Asia and the Pacific. The decision was taken at the 11th session of the register held in Jakarta, Indonesia. With this recognition, India’s total number of inscriptions in the regional register has risen to six. The three works represent different aspects of India’s knowledge traditions. Rajatarangini is a historical account of Kashmir, the Mahabharata explores Dharma, duty and human values, while Arthashastra deals with governance, diplomacy and statecraft. This recognition is a matter of pride for India’s civilisational continuity, its rich knowledge traditions and its contribution to the world. The development was announced by Member Secretary, Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA),  Dr. Sachchidanand Joshi which played an important role in preparing the nomination dossiers for all three works.

. In the Indian bullion market today, 24 carat gold dropped 2.3 per cent to 1,31,164 rupees per 10 grams. Meanwhile, silver also declined 3.2 per cent to 1,63, 733 rupees per kilogram according to the closing rates of India Bullion and Jewellers Association.

. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare has proposed the incorporation of Good Storage and Distribution Practices (GSDP) guidelines for pharmaceutical products into the Drugs Rules, 1945. The Ministry said that the proposal aims to ensure that the quality, safety, efficacy and integrity of pharmaceutical products are maintained throughout the distribution chain.The proposed framework builds upon the GSDP guidance developed by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation. The guidelines seek to ensure the quality and identity of pharmaceutical products at every stage of the distribution process. The Ministry said that maintaining appropriate storage and distribution conditions is essential to preserving the quality and integrity of pharmaceutical products beyond the manufacturing stage. The proposed framework seeks to address potential risks associated with their handling and movement across the supply chain.The Ministry said that the incorporation of this requirement into the Drugs Rules, 1945, is expected to strengthen the regulatory framework governing pharmaceutical distribution and support effective regulatory oversight, inspection and enforcement by the Central and State drug-control authorities. The proposed guidelines will further strengthen assurance that pharmaceutical products remain within specified quality and environmental conditions during storage and transportation, thereby reducing the risk of deterioration, contamination, mix-ups, falsification, diversion and unauthorised distribution.Stakeholders and members of the public are invited to submit their objections and suggestions, if any, to the Under Secretary (Drugs Regulation), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare or via email at drugsdiv-mohfw@gov.in.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has asked industries to make ‘India First’ the foundation for every long-term investment decision they take over the next 20 years. He said, this will lead to a self-reliant nation and also open up new opportunities for the growth of their business.Mr Modi was addressing the centenary convention of Industry body FICCI in New Delhi today. He said, over the course of its 100 years, FICCI has witnessed the nation’s industry achieve a great deal. The Prime Minister said, now it is the time to determine what Indian industry can achieve over the next 20 years. He said, over the past 100 years, India’s economy has witnessed many phases.Mr Modi said, people saw the License Quota Raj, the failed experiment of nationalisation and a time in the 21st century when India’s economy was counted among the Fragile Five. The Prime Minister said, however, in the last 12 years, the youth, farmers, workers, and industry leaders have worked hard to transform this situation.He said, today, India is the world’s fastest-growing major economy, projected to grow at around seven per cent. Mr Modi said, last month, India’s goods exports reached nearly 50 billion dollars, its highest-ever monthly goods export. The Prime Minister said, it is due to India’s strong performance that agencies like Moody’s Ratings, S&P Global Ratings, Fitch Ratings, the World Bank, and the Asian Development Bank (ADB) are revising the growth forecasts upward.Mr Modi said, the latest World Bank report states that in just 12-13 years, 50 crore Indians have been lifted out of poverty. He said, in the 1970s, when the ‘Garibi Hatao’ slogan was given, India’s population was around 50 crore and poverty could have been eradicated then too.The Prime Minister said, but FICCI is a witness that there was a flaw in policies and unfortunately, a lack of the right intention. He said, when Government worked with the right policies and the right intention, 50 crore poor people came out of poverty in just 12-13 years. Mr Modi said, this shows that the pace and the path on which India is moving today are right, accurate, and hold the guarantee of the nation’s success.Encouraging industry to leverage India’s recent trade agreements, the Prime Minister urged businesses to invest in understanding global customer needs, meeting standards, and building distribution networks. He added that the domestic market should not be the comfort zone, as it must give the confidence to compete in global markets.Emphasising that a nation progresses by honouring farmers, small entrepreneurs, industry, wealth creators, and taxpayers, the Prime Minister listed the pro-business and taxpayer-friendly reforms taken by his government. It includes cutting the basic corporate tax rate from 30 percent in 2014 to 22 percent, exempting income up to 12 lakh rupees to boost purchasing power, simplifying returns and refunds, and lowering GST rates on numerous goods to stimulate demand.Congratulating FICCI on completing 100 years since its inception, Mr Modi said, for an organization to remain consistently vigilant and active for a hundred years, evolving with the changing times and continuing to play its part in the nation’s economic journey is a remarkable achievement.

. Petroleum and Natural Gas Minister Hardeep Singh Puri has called for greater indigenisation and self-reliance in the country’s oil and gas equipment sector to strengthen domestic manufacturing and boost exports.During an industry interaction with members of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) in New Delhi yesterday, the Minister stressed the need to develop and manufacture advanced technologies and equipment within the country. He emphasised that India must move beyond import substitution towards developing world-class indigenous technologies, strengthening domestic supply chains and emerging as a global manufacturing and export hub for oil and gas equipment. He said country’s expanding energy infrastructure offers significant opportunities for domestic manufacturers.The Minister said that initiatives such as GOBARdhan, and the Samudra Manthan Mission are expected to open up new opportunities in Compressed Bio-Gas, offshore exploration, specialised equipment and advanced engineering. Mr Puri called upon Oil and Gas Public Sector Undertakings to partner with Indian manufacturers, promote technology development, facilitate field trials and provide greater opportunities to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.

. The nationwide ‘Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad: Know Your Vote’ campaign has concluded with 536 Yuva Samvads conducted across 31 States and Union Territories. The campaign organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports through Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat) reached over one lakh young people and involved more than 5000 Youth Icons. The campaign brought discussions on electoral awareness to colleges and educational institutions across the country. It encouraged young people, particularly first-time voters, to understand their voting rights and electoral procedures and participate responsibly in democracy.The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the campaign witnessed participation by Governors, Union Ministers, State Ministers, Members of Parliament and other public representatives. It added that sports personalities and youth icons from the sporting community also participated in programmes, sharing their experiences and encouraging youth participation in sports.The Yuva Samvads provided young participants with opportunities to seek clarity on electoral procedures, discuss voting rights and civic responsibilities, and interact directly with public representatives and Youth Icons.

. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has highlighted the strong complementarities between Indian innovation and Italian enterprise, stressing the vast potential for collaboration in sectors such as semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI) and automobiles. Addressing the plenary session of the Fourth India-Italy Business and Innovation Forum in Rome, alongside Italy’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani, Goyal urged businesses from both countries to look beyond traditional trade and explore new avenues of economic and technological cooperation. He also highlighted India’s development achievements, noting that 496 million people had been lifted out of extreme poverty in just 12 years.Interacting with startups at the India-Italy Innovation Forum, he said he had heard from entrepreneurs on both sides about how they developed their ideas and built businesses around them. He encouraged Indian and Italian startups to explore partnerships in each other’s markets to expand their reach and accelerate growth. Emphasising the importance of such platforms for young entrepreneurs, Goyal said opportunities like these could open doors to major business breakthroughs.Reaffirming the commitment to strengthen bilateral economic ties, Goyal said that with expanding opportunities for businesses, startups and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), both countries are working towards achieving their bilateral trade target of 20 billion euros by 2029. He expressed confidence that the growing economic engagement would take the India-Italy partnership to the next level.

. In Football, defending champions India will take on Pakistan in the final of the SAFF Championship at the National Stadium in Dhaka, Bangladesh, today. India will be aiming to secure their 10th overall SAFF Championship title and make history by winning the tournament for the third consecutive time. The Blue Tigers booked their place in the final after defeating Bhutan 2-1 in the semi-final on Saturday.Pakistan, meanwhile, will be making their first-ever appearance in a SAFF Championship final. The two sides have met 30 times in senior internationals, with India winning 17 matches, Pakistan four and nine ending in draws. Today’s clash will, however, be their first meeting in a senior SAFF Championship final.India are the most successful team in the tournament’s history, having won a record nine titles, and they are the favourites to lift the trophy once again.

. The Indian Air Force and Central Sanskrit University ,New Delhi have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to facilitate access to structured learning and certification opportunities in Yoga for Agniveervayu. The signing ceremony was held at Air Headquarters and was chaired by Air Officer-in-charge Personnel. The MOU was signed by the Assistant Chief of the Air Staff (education) and the Vice-chancellor of Central Sanskrit University.

. In Mizoram, three-day Leitlangpui Music Festival is underway in south Mizoram’s Lunglei town, bringing together established musicians, emerging bands and local entrepreneurs to showcase the state’s musical heritage and promote tourism. Organised by the Ministry of Tourism and Mizoram Tourism department, the festival began yesterday at Lena Stadium at Serkawn under the theme “Music Comes Home to Serkawn”. The festival seeks to connect that legacy with contemporary musicians and emerging talent.Addressing the inaugural ceremony, Tourism Minister Lalnghinglova Hmar said music was an inseparable part of Mizoram’s cultural identity and Serkawn held a special place in the state’s musical history. The minister said that the government aimed to take Mizoram’s music and cultural heritage to national and international audiences while creating opportunities for young artists, entrepreneurs and local communities. The festival features performances by established and emerging Mizo musicians.The second day includes a band competition with 10 finalists from Aizawl, Lunglei, Nagaland and Assam, while winners of the previous two editions, Swordtune and Knot, are also scheduled to perform. The final day will feature performances by several Mizo artists and bands, followed by the minister’s address and a fireworks display.

. In Football, India clinched a record-extending 10th SAFF Championship title, beating arch-rivals Pakistan 2-1 in a thrilling final to retain their crown at the National Stadium in Dhaka last night.The Blue Tigers also made history by winning the tournament for the third consecutive time. For India, Suhail Ahmad Bhat in 60th and Sandip Mandi in 88th minute scored goals. India had booked their place in the final after defeating Bhutan 2-1 in the semi-final on Saturday.Union Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya has congratulated the Indian men’s football team for winning a historic hat-trick of SAFF Championship titles in Dhaka. Congratulating the team on social media, Dr. Mandaviya hailed the achievement and praised the players for completing a hat-trick of consecutive titles.

. Union Home Minister Amit Shah inaugurated the 6th Anti-Terror Conference in New Delhi today. The two-day anti-terror conference is organised by the National Investigation Agency under the Ministry of Home Affairs to strengthen the country’s collective response to evolving terrorist threats.Subjects like, obtaining evidence from foreign jurisdictions, the application of digital forensics and data analysis in counter-terrorism investigations and effective management of trials, will be discussed during the conference. Sessions will also cover countering radicalisation, espionage, and emerging hybrid threats to national security.

. The International Cricket Council (ICC) Board has approved the windows for major men’s events until 2035, confirming that India will host the 2029 Champions Trophy and co-host the 2031 ODI World Cup with Bangladesh.The 2029 Champions Trophy will be held in India from 9th to 28th of October, while the 2031 ODI World Cup will take place from 9th October to 23rd November, jointly hosted by India and Bangladesh.The ICC also announced the dates for tournaments beyond 2031, although the host nations are yet to be confirmed. The schedule covers major events from the 2028 T20 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand to the 2035 ODI World Cup.The 2028 T20 World Cup will run from October 12 to  November 12. The next edition will be held in 2030, with England, Scotland and Ireland jointly hosting the tournament. The 2032 and 2034 editions are also scheduled, but their venues are yet to be announced.Meanwhile, the World Test Championship (WTC) Final will continue to be held every two years in June until 2035. England will host the 2029 and 2031 finals, while the hosts for the 2033 and 2035 editions are yet to be decided.

. The India Meteorological Centre says severe cyclonic storm Akvan is continuing over the west-central Bay of Bengal and has moved at a speed of 5 kilometres per hour during the last 6 hours. The storm is likely to cross the North Andhra Pradesh and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri by tomorrow afternoon.Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan is likely to bring moderate to heavy rain at some parts of Srikakulam district today. Moderate rain is also likely at some places in Vizianagaram, Parvathipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitarama Raju, Polavaram, Visakhapatnam and Anakapalli districts.Civil Aviation Minister K. Ram Mohan Naidu has urged people in North Andhra Pradesh to remain alert and take precautionary measures. Farmers in Srikakulam have been asked to cover harvested paddy with tarpaulins and move it to safer places, if needed.The Andhra Pradesh government has put the administration on high alert. NDRF teams, SDRF teams and local fire service teams have been kept ready for emergency operations. Precautionary measures are being taken to prevent damage to power infrastructure due to strong winds along the coastal belt. People in cyclone-prone areas have been advised to remain alert and follow the instructions issued by the authorities.

. India and Japan have agreed to fast-track defence agreements related to the Unified Complex Radio Antenna or UNICORN  stealth naval mast project to strengthen maritime security cooperation and expand joint defence manufacturing following their 2+2 ministerial dialogue in Tokyo.Addressing a joint press briefing alongside External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said the discussions covered a wide range of bilateral and regional issues under the two countries’ Special Strategic and Global Partnership.Mr. Singh said the talks built on the Joint Declaration on Security Cooperation signed in August 2025, as India and Japan prepare to mark 75 years of diplomatic relations in 2027.Highlighting progress in defence ties, he welcomed the first-ever participation of Japan Air Self-Defense Force fighter aircraft in the bilateral air exercise Veer Guardian 2026 in India and the third India-Japan Defence Industry Forum held in Tokyo on October 13. Both sides also advanced discussions on air and space domain awareness.On maritime security, the two countries agreed to implement their recently signed Memorandum of Arrangement through cooperation in maritime and air domain awareness, search and rescue, and information sharing. They also called for an early conclusion of an agreement allowing reciprocal access to ship repair facilities and agreed to enhance cooperation in mine countermeasure capabilities. Mr. Singh further stressed the need to expedite agreements related to UNICORN, the joint stealth naval mast development initiative, and expand defence industrial collaboration under the ‘Design with Japan, Make in India’ framework, including cooperation in niche, underwater and missile technologies.External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said that India-Japan cooperation aims to support a multipolar Asia and a multipolar world, stressing the need for stronger bilateral ties amid growing geopolitical and economic uncertainties. Speaking after the fourth India-Japan 2+2 Foreign and Defence Ministerial Dialogue in Tokyo, Mr. Jaishankar highlighted the two countries’ longstanding friendship and their potential to play a greater role in shaping the global order. He also reaffirmed India’s and Japan’s commitment, alongside their Quad partners, to maintaining a free and open Indo-Pacific.Raising concerns over the growing weaponisation of connectivity, natural resources, services, supply chains and market access, he stressed the need to build resilience and explore alternatives. He particularly highlighted vulnerabilities linked to connectivity and maritime choke points following recent developments in the Gulf. He said, the discussions also covered the changing nature of warfare, including the increasing use of smart weapons and innovative technologies. Mr. Jaishankar said cooperation in these areas would complement the broader India-Japan partnership in innovation and startups.

. Under the theme ‘Vikas Aur Virasat’ (Development and Heritage), women-led Self-Help Groups (SHGs) from Tripura, along with various wings under the Department of Industries and Commerce, are participating in the international trade fair being held in New Delhi.At the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, the Tripura Pavilion is showcasing a wide range of products manufactured by the state’s Self-Help Groups, along with an impressive collection of bamboo and cane handicrafts.Tripura Industries and Commerce Minister Santana Chakma visited the state’s stalls and encouraged the women entrepreneurs, appreciating their efforts. She said their contribution is significant in strengthening Tripura’s economy. She further stated that participation in such fairs would help promote products manufactured in Tripura and increase their recognition in the global market.It may be mentioned that Union Minister for Commerce and Industry Piyush Goyal inaugurated the fair on November 13. The exhibition will continue until November 27, with participation from representatives of more than 30 states and Union Territories across the country.

. Chairman of Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Tuhin Kanta Pandey today said country’s capital markets have undergone a remarkable transformation over the past decade. Addressing the 65th annual general meeting of World Federation of Exchanges in Mumbai, Mr. Pandey said that country’s equity market capitalisation has grown at around 16 percent annually over the past decade and stands at approximately 5 trillion US dollars. He said that country has over 6700 listed companies and the market-capitalisation-to-GDP ratio stood around 130 percent.The SEBI Chairman said that companies have raised an average of about 130 billion US dollars annually through equity and debt issuances in the past decade. Talking about reform, Mr. Pandey said the regulator has reduced listing timelines and enabled the issuance of debt securities in the corporate bond market with a face value as low as ten thousand rupees. SEBI Chairman said artificial intelligence and advanced analytics offer significant opportunities in market surveillance, risk monitoring, regulatory compliance and investor services. On the other hand, Mr. Pandey said cyber threats, technological dependencies, market volatility and cross-border financial linkages affect exchanges and clearing corporations across jurisdictions.

. In Men’s Cricket, an unbeaten 173-run stand between Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips took host New Zealand to 243 at the loss of 5 wickets at stumps on Day 1 of the first Test against India at the Basin Reserve in Wellington today.Nicholls, who slammed his 12th Test century, finished unbeaten on 113, while Phillips will resume his innings on 94 on Day 2. For India, Jasprit Bumrah scalped 3 wickets, while Anshul Kamboj and Akash Deep took one wicket each.Earlier, India won the toss and opted to bowl.

. Political unrest and violence continue to intensify across Bangladesh, with fresh incidents of arson, crude bomb explosions, vandalism and political clashes reported in several districts on Wednesday night and early Thursday. At the same time, authorities have stepped up arrests of Awami League leaders and activists as the party faces a ban on its activities.Former Education Minister and senior Awami League leader Nurul Islam Nahid was detained from Dhaka’s Uttara area around 2:20 am on Thursday, police said.In Chattogram, the ancestral residence of former interim government Chief Adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus caught fire in a suspected petrol bomb attack. No casualties were reported.In Gopalganj, the residence of lawmaker KM Babor was vandalised and set on fire following crude bomb explosions. In Gazipur, a fire broke out at a Palli Bidyut complaint centre after suspected petrol containers were thrown inside.Meanwhile, two BRTC buses were torched in Rajshahi, and a section of railway track was set on fire in Charghat, disrupting train services for about an hour.In Tangail’s Mirzapur, a memorial dedicated to those killed during the July uprising was set ablaze, while several crude bombs exploded nearby.In Narail, two BNP leaders, Shahin and Sohel Molla, died after an attack on a BNP procession in Kalia. According to police and local media reports, the procession was organised to protest against the prevailing situation. The alleged involvement of Awami League activists has been reported, but the circumstances and those responsible are yet to be independently established.The developments underscore mounting political tensions and growing security concerns in Bangladesh amid continuing political confrontation and intensified law-enforcement operations.

. External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will co chair the fourth India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministers’ Dialogue, also known as the 2+2 Dialogue with their Japanese counterparts, Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizum in Tokyo today.Earlier yesterday, addressing the inaugural Raisina Tokyo 2026 event, Dr. Jaishankar called for deeper India-Japan cooperation in key sectors, including semiconductors, critical minerals, clean energy, advanced manufacturing and defence. He stressed the importance of trusted partnerships, supply chain diversification and stronger national capacities amid a rapidly changing global landscape. He said stronger bilateral ties would contribute to peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific and strengthen the foundations of a multipolar Asia and world.Dr Jaishankar also addressed the 9th India-Japan Indo-Pacific Forum being held in New Delhi through video message yesterday. He described India and Japan as indispensable partners in shaping a free, open and rules-based Indo-Pacific. He said their Special Strategic and Global Partnership, anchored in trust, goodwill and a common strategic outlook, contributes to peace, stability and economic prosperity for both countries and the wider world.

. Ace Indian shuttlers, Lakshya Sen and Kidambi Srikanth advanced to the Men’s Singles second round of Hong Kong Open Badminton Championships today. In the opening round, Srikanth defeated Japan’s Koki Watanabe 21-16, 16-21, 21-9 while Lakshya beat France’s Arnaud Merklé 14-21, 21-16, 25-23.In Women’s Singles, Rakshitha Ramraj and Ashmita Chaliha also advanced to the second round. Rakshitha defeated Mia Blichfeldt 21-18, 21-18 while Ashmita defeated compatriot Isharani Baruah 12-21, 21-13, 21-12 in the round of 32.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices ended over 0.6 per cent lower today, snapping their two-day rally. The Sensex declined 500 points to close at 82,032. The Nifty lost 159 points to settle at 25,228.In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index shed 1.2 per cent, and the Smallcap 100 index dropped 0.4 per cent.In the Sensex pack, 22 out of 30 constituent companies logged losses. Among the top underperformers, Titan plunged 4.8 per cent, TCS dropped two and a half per cent and Bajaj Finance as well as Eternal shed nearly two and a half per cent. In contrast, SBI rose 2.3 per cent, ITC gained 1.4 per cent and Ultratech Cement added 1.2 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 25 out of 28 sectors edged downward. Among the top laggards, Consumer Durables lost over 3.1 per cent, Metal declined 2.2 per cent and Mid-Small Private Banks Quality Tilt fell one and a half per cent. In contrast, PSU Bank as well as Telecommunication rose 0.3 per cent, and Healthcare eked out a marginal gain.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2,924 companies declined, 1,512 advanced and 209 remained unchanged.
